title: Online Event Ticket Sales
one_liner: Digital marketplaces sell, distribute and resell tickets for concerts, sports, theater, festivals and other live events.
overview: Online event ticket sales covers primary ticketing platforms, secondary resale marketplaces and self-service event tools that let consumers discover, buy, store, transfer and resell tickets online or through mobile apps. The 2025 market is materially larger than the older IBIS operator-revenue baseline because many current market estimates report gross merchandise value, including ticket face value and fees, while IBIS measured industry revenue earned by ticket sellers. Current 2025-2026 conditions show solid but no longer explosive growth: Live Nation's Ticketmaster remained the dominant primary ticketing platform, StubHub became a public company in 2025, Eventbrite went private in 2026, and federal regulators moved aggressively against hidden fees, bot-enabled resale and Live Nation-Ticketmaster market power.

key_stats.market_size: 2025 US online event ticketing market estimated at $18.0 billion to $18.21 billion in gross merchandise/value terms; 2026 implied market size is about $18.9 billion to $19.1 billion using the 2025-2033 CAGR range.
key_stats.growth: 2025-2033 US CAGR estimated at 5.07%; global online event ticketing market expected to grow from $53.04 billion in 2025 to $56.58 billion in 2026, up 6.7%.
key_stats.mobile_share: 2025 mobile accounted for about 55% to 58.4% of global online event ticketing transactions in market-research estimates.
key_stats.ticketmaster_scale: 2025 Live Nation ticketing revenue was $3.1 billion, fee-bearing GTV was $37.1 billion, and Ticketmaster sold 346 million fee-bearing tickets plus about 300 million non-fee-bearing tickets.
key_stats.stubhub_scale: 2025 StubHub gross merchandise sales were $9.2 billion, up 6% year over year, while revenue was $1.745 billion, down 1%.
key_stats.eventbrite_scale: 2025 Eventbrite creators hosted nearly 4.6 million events, issued 258 million tickets and generated more than $3.0 billion of gross ticket sales globally.

baseline_2022.market_size: Approximately $6.6 billion in 2022 operator revenue, inferred from the baseline IBIS 2021 revenue of $6.309 billion and its 2021-2026 projected annual growth rate of about 4.7%.
baseline_2022.growth: Baseline projected 2021-2026 industry revenue CAGR of about 4.7%, after estimated 2021 growth of 14.7% from the 2020 COVID-19 collapse.
baseline_2022.basis: IBIS baseline uses industry revenue/fees in 2021 dollars, not ticket gross merchandise value.

how_it_makes_money: Platforms earn money from convenience fees, order processing fees, buyer and seller resale fees, ticketing software and venue-client services, payment and fulfillment fees, promoted listings, event marketing tools, advertising, data products, insurance referrals, VIP packages and ancillary add-ons. Primary platforms usually collect fees on behalf of venues, promoters and teams; resale marketplaces monetize liquidity between sellers and buyers; self-service tools monetize independent creators through ticketing, marketing and subscription-like event tools.
cost_structure: Major costs include payment processing, fraud prevention, cloud hosting, app and platform engineering, customer support, chargebacks, ticket replacement and fulfillment, sales commissions, venue and promoter contract advances, consumer acquisition marketing, search and social advertising, compliance, litigation and general overhead. Large incumbents have high fixed technology and contract costs but strong operating leverage when ticket volume rises; resale and self-service platforms carry heavier variable costs from digital marketing, payment processing and buyer guarantees.
current_dynamics: Demand remains supported by concerts, sports and experiential spending, but growth is normalizing after the 2021-2024 reopening surge. Stadium concerts and premium sports inventory are producing high transaction values, while smaller venues and some non-concert categories face softer volume and price sensitivity. Competitive dynamics are shaped less by pure software features than by exclusive venue contracts, artist/promoter relationships, inventory access, resale liquidity, fraud controls, mobile wallet integration and consumer trust. Regulation has become a central operating issue: all-in pricing rules, bot enforcement, resale scrutiny and the Live Nation-Ticketmaster antitrust case are pushing platforms to make fees more transparent and ticket limits more enforceable.
whats_growing: Mobile-first ticketing, wallet-based entry, secure transfer, dynamic pricing, premium packages, verified resale, stadium tours, sports ticketing, AI-driven discovery, creator marketing tools, timed-entry events, fraud prevention, identity verification and all-in price displays are growing. Platforms with exclusive supply, trusted buyer guarantees and high-intent consumer traffic are capturing the most value.
whats_shrinking: Paper and print-at-home tickets, phone and box-office sales, hidden-fee checkout flows, lightly policed broker activity, fragmented small resale sites, pandemic-era virtual-only event ticketing and lower-margin undifferentiated ticketing software are shrinking. Some resale marketplaces also saw pressure in 2025 from lower take rates, weaker marketplace revenue and higher customer acquisition costs.
recent_developments: 2024-05-23: The US Department of Justice and state attorneys general sued Live Nation and Ticketmaster over alleged monopolization in live concerts and primary ticketing.
2025-05-12: The FTC's Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees took effect for live-event tickets, requiring advertised prices to include mandatory fees upfront.
2025-09-17: StubHub began trading on the NYSE after pricing its IPO at $23.50 per share and raising about $758.0 million in net proceeds.
2025-09-18: The FTC and seven states sued Live Nation and Ticketmaster over alleged illegal resale tactics, bait-and-switch pricing and ticket-limit deception.
2026-02: Live Nation reported 2025 Ticketing revenue of $3.1 billion, 346 million fee-bearing tickets and $37.1 billion of fee-bearing GTV.
2026-03-10: Eventbrite completed its sale to Bending Spoons at $4.50 per share and ceased operating as a public company.
outlook: The US market should keep expanding through 2026 and beyond, but at a mid-single-digit pace rather than the rebound rates seen immediately after reopening. Growth will come from more live events, higher average transaction values, mobile conversion, premium experiences and stronger resale controls. Margin upside depends on marketing efficiency, fee transparency compliance and platform scale; downside risks include consumer backlash against high fees, softer discretionary spending, artist cancellations, antitrust remedies, resale restrictions and higher fraud-prevention costs.
themes: Regulatory pressure on Ticketmaster and resale markets
Self-service ticketing for creators and local events

one_sentence: The US online event ticket sales industry has moved from post-pandemic recovery into a more mature, mobile-first market where growth is driven by live-event demand, high-value concert and sports inventory, resale liquidity, pricing tools and regulatory pressure for clearer fees.

title: Online Eyeglasses & Contact Lens Sales
one_liner: Online optical retailers sell prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, readers and contact lenses through DTC websites, apps and marketplace-style storefronts, competing on price, convenience, virtual try-on and prescription portability.
overview: This industry includes retailers that sell eyeglasses, prescription lenses, sunglasses, readers and contact lenses primarily through online storefronts and mobile apps. Demand is tied to replacement cycles, prescription updates, contact lens replenishment, digital shopping adoption, vision insurance workflows and the aging US population. The channel grew rapidly through the 2020 pandemic shift to e-commerce, then normalized as shoppers returned to stores, but online remains structurally stronger because consumers increasingly expect virtual try-on, remote prescription renewal, home delivery, subscription replenishment and lower prices than traditional optical retail.

key_stats.market_size: 2025 tracked US online contact lens and eyewear revenue was $1.68 billion.
key_stats.growth: 2025 tracked online revenue was down 0% to 5% from 2024; 2026 tracked online revenue is forecast to grow 10% to 20%.
key_stats.addressable_market: The US optical industry reached $69.5 billion in 2025, up 4.4% from 2024.
key_stats.consumer_base: About 94% of US adults, more than 250 million people, used prescription or non-prescription eyewear in 2025.
key_stats.warby_parker_scale: Warby Parker reported 2025 net revenue of $871.9 million, up 13.0% from 2024, and Q1 2026 revenue of $242.4 million, up 8.3% from Q1 2025.
key_stats.warby_parker_2026_guidance: Warby Parker guided 2026 net revenue to $959 million to $976 million, about 10% to 12% above 2025.

baseline_2022.market_size: IBISWorld baseline revenue was about $1.0 billion in 2022, in 2020 dollars.
baseline_2022.growth: IBISWorld baseline 2022 annual revenue growth was 0.4%, after 2017-2022 revenue CAGR of 8.2%.
baseline_2022.profit: IBISWorld baseline profit was $50 million in 2020, with a 3.2% profit margin in 2020.
baseline_2022.forecast: IBISWorld baseline forecast revenue was $1.2 billion in 2027, with 2022-2027 CAGR of 2.3%.

how_it_makes_money: Revenue comes from online sales of frames, prescription lenses, lens upgrades, sunglasses, readers, contact lenses, accessories, expedited shipping, subscription or auto-replenishment contact lens orders, and in some cases telehealth-style prescription renewal, virtual vision testing, in-person eye exams tied to omnichannel brands, insurance reimbursements and managed vision care transactions.
cost_structure: The main costs are product sourcing, lens manufacturing or lab processing, contact lens procurement, prescription verification workflows, fulfillment, shipping, returns, payment processing, digital marketing, search and social acquisition, customer service, technology, software, data security, insurance administration and corporate overhead. Warby Parker reported 2025 cost of goods sold equal to 46.0% of revenue and 2025 SG&A equal to 54.6% of revenue, with gross margin pressured by tariffs, contact lens mix, optical lab costs, doctor headcount and shipping costs.
current_dynamics: The industry is shifting from pure discount e-commerce toward omnichannel optical care. Online-only operators still win on convenience and price, but larger retailers are blending stores, eye exams, digital prescription tools and e-commerce to reduce friction. 2025 optical spending rose even as unit volumes fell, showing that price increases, premium lenses and higher-value purchases offset more cautious consumer behavior. Prescription-release rules remain central because online sellers need consumers to obtain and transfer valid prescriptions from prescribers. Tariffs, shipping costs and contact lens mix are pressuring margins, while AI glasses and virtual try-on are increasing technology investment by better-capitalized brands.
whats_growing: Contact lens replenishment, daily disposable and specialty lenses, progressive lenses, lens enhancements, virtual try-on, remote prescription renewal, insurance-enabled checkout, mobile ordering, omnichannel fulfillment, AI-enabled eyewear development and online retailers with strong repeat-purchase flows are growing in 2025-2026.
whats_shrinking: Purely transactional online eyewear without prescription support, low-margin contact lens resellers, undifferentiated frame marketplaces, retailers exposed to high paid-search costs, and weaker sites with falling traffic or conversion are shrinking or losing share; tracked online sales for the broader contact lens and eyewear set declined 0% to 5% in 2025 before the expected 2026 rebound.
recent_developments: 2024-06: The FTC finalized Eyeglass Rule updates requiring stronger proof that prescribers give patients free eyeglass prescriptions after refractive exams.
2025-01: The Vision Council estimated the US optical industry at $69.5 billion for 2025, up 4.4% from 2024, despite lower product volumes.
2025-12: Warby Parker reported 2025 net revenue of $871.9 million, up 13.0% from 2024, with gross margin of 54.0%.
2026-03: Warby Parker reported Q1 2026 revenue of $242.4 million, up 8.3% from Q1 2025, and reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $959 million to $976 million.
2026-05: Grips estimated 2025 online contact lens and eyewear revenue across tracked retailers at $1.68 billion and forecast 2026 growth of 10% to 20%.
2026-06: The FTC again highlighted Eyeglass Rule and Contact Lens Rule enforcement, warning prescribers that prescriptions must be released at no extra charge.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is positive but uneven. Industry revenue should recover from a soft 2025 as prescription refresh cycles, contact lens replenishment and digital adoption support demand, but growth will skew toward brands that combine online checkout with exam access, prescription management, insurance integration and trusted fulfillment. Margin expansion will be difficult where retailers rely on paid acquisition, absorb shipping and returns, or sell lower-margin contact lenses. Longer term, AI glasses and connected eyewear may expand the category, but near-term winners will be operators that convert recurring vision needs into repeat online orders while staying compliant with prescription rules.
themes: Virtual try-on and remote vision testing
Premium lenses and higher average order values
one_sentence: The US online eyeglasses and contact lens channel is a small but strategically important slice of the optical market, with 2025 tracked online revenue of about $1.68 billion after a slight 2025 decline and a 2026 rebound forecast of roughly 10% to 20%.

title: Online Flower Shops
one_liner: U.S. online flower shops sell flowers, plants and bundled gifts through websites and apps, using owned fulfillment, direct-from-farm shipping and local florist networks.
overview: Online flower shops take orders and payments online for cut flowers, arranged bouquets, potted plants, gift baskets and floral-network services, then fulfill through local florists, direct-shipment farms, distribution centers or owned retail locations. The 2020 IBISWorld baseline described a growth-stage industry that had shifted demand away from brick-and-mortar florists, with 2020 revenue of $5.16 billion and a 2020-2025 forecast to $5.7 billion. Current 2025-2026 market indicators point to a bifurcated picture: the broader U.S. floral gifting market is still expanding, while large online-first operators are dealing with lower order volume, less efficient digital marketing, and tighter consumer spending.

key_stats.market_size: U.S. online flower delivery tracked GMV was $712 million in 2025 across 70+ tracked retailers; broader U.S. floral gifting market was $12.55 billion in 2025; U.S. flower delivery service revenue was $1.733 billion in 2025 and estimated at $1.834 billion in 2026.
key_stats.growth: Tracked online flower delivery revenue declined 10-20% in 2025 and was forecast to grow 10-20% in 2026; U.S. flower delivery service revenue is forecast to grow at a 6.5% CAGR from 2026 to 2033; broader U.S. floral gifting is forecast at a 5.25% CAGR from 2025 to 2031.
key_stats.public_leader_scale: 1-800-FLOWERS.COM reported FY2025 revenue of $1.686 billion, down 8.0% from FY2024; its Consumer Floral & Gifts segment was $776.8 million in FY2025, down 8.6%.
key_stats.online_channel_signal: 1-800-FLOWERS.COM e-commerce revenue was $1.464 billion in FY2025, down 9.3% from FY2024.
key_stats.profitability_signal: 1-800-FLOWERS.COM FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was $29.2 million versus $93.1 million in FY2024; FY2026 company guidance as of May 7, 2026 was adjusted EBITDA around breakeven plus or minus $2 million.

baseline_2022.market_size: Approximately $5.36 billion in 2022, derived from the IBISWorld baseline report's 2020 revenue of $5.16 billion and 2020-2025 projected 2.0% CAGR.
baseline_2022.growth: About 2.0% forecast annualized growth for 2020-2025 in the IBISWorld baseline; the baseline did not separately report actual 2022 growth.
baseline_2022.context: The baseline expected revenue to recover after a 2020 pandemic decline and not surpass pre-pandemic levels until 2023.

how_it_makes_money: Revenue comes from online sales of potted plants, arranged cut flowers, unarranged cut flowers, floral gift baskets and add-ons, delivery and service fees, subscriptions, corporate gifting, and network or wire-service fees charged to local florists for order routing, marketing, payment processing and related services.
cost_structure: Major costs are flower and plant purchasing, florist fulfillment, packaging, spoilage and replacements, last-mile delivery, freight, customer service labor, technology, payment processing, and digital marketing. The baseline report estimated 2020 profit margin at 3.8% and forecast 2025 profit margin at 6.6%, but 2025-2026 public-company results show pressure from merchandise costs, tariffs, marketing inefficiency, fixed-cost deleveraging and lower order volume.
current_dynamics: Demand is still tied to birthdays, sympathy, Mother's Day, Valentine's Day, weddings and corporate occasions, but the category is increasingly shaped by mobile ordering, same-day delivery, curated bundles, subscriptions and self-gifting. At the same time, inflation-sensitive consumers are trading down or substituting groceries, chocolate, cards and other gifts, while online operators face expensive customer acquisition and changing search-result pages. Large platforms are emphasizing pricing discipline, fulfillment quality, loyalty programs, cost savings and third-party distribution rather than pure order growth.
whats_growing: Same-day and next-day delivery, app-based ordering, premium bouquets, potted plants, personalized arrangements, subscriptions, self-gifting, corporate gifting, bundled flowers with wine, chocolate or cards, and hybrid online-plus-local retail models are gaining traction in 2025-2026.
whats_shrinking: Lower-margin wire-service volumes, generic unarranged cut-flower demand, inefficient paid-search-driven orders, discount-heavy promotions, and discretionary everyday gifting from value-conscious households are under pressure. Public leader data also shows 2025-2026 weakness in Consumer Floral & Gifts revenue and BloomNet network revenue.
recent_developments: 2025-09-04: 1-800-FLOWERS.COM reported FY2025 revenue of $1.686 billion, down 8.0%, with Consumer Floral & Gifts down 8.6% to $776.8 million.
2025-12-08: The Bouqs Co. partnered with UPS-owned Roadie for same-day delivery in key markets and planned for a 44% Q4 order-volume increase versus Q3.
2026-01-21: The Bouqs Co. launched a Regulation Crowdfunding raise of up to $5 million to fund retail expansion and its farm-to-door model.
2026-01-30: Teleflora launched its 2026 Valentine's Day campaign and bouquet lineup to stimulate peak-season demand.
2026-05-07: 1-800-FLOWERS.COM reported FY2026 Q3 revenue down 11.6%, Consumer Floral & Gifts down 18.7%, and guided FY2026 revenue down 10-12%.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is cautious for online-only incumbents but constructive for the category over a multi-year period. Near term, sales remain exposed to discretionary spending, marketing costs, tariffs, florist fulfillment costs and traffic shifts from search engines. Medium term, online flower shops should benefit from the broader floral gifting market's projected 5.25% CAGR from 2025 to 2031, provided operators improve repeat purchase economics, expand local same-day coverage and differentiate through quality, personalization and bundles.
sources: Baseline file: /home/manishmehta/ui-projects/ibis-industries/txt_full/online-flower-shops.txt, IBISWorld Online Flower Shops, last updated 2020-11-30
one_sentence: The industry remains structurally supported by e-commerce, same-day delivery and personalized gifting, but 2025-2026 performance is mixed as weaker discretionary demand, higher fulfillment costs and paid-search pressure weigh on leading online floral brands.

title: Online Gambling Services in the US
one_liner: Legal online betting has scaled from a post-PASPA land grab into a concentrated, mobile-first gambling market led by FanDuel and DraftKings.
overview: The industry operates licensed digital platforms that let eligible users place sports wagers, play online casino games, enter poker games and use related real-money wagering products inside state borders. The market remains state-by-state because federal law and state gaming statutes limit where bets can be accepted, while geolocation, payments, identity checks and responsible-gaming controls are core operating requirements. After the 2018 PASPA repeal opened the sports-betting market, revenue expanded rapidly as states legalized mobile wagering and national brands spent heavily on customer acquisition. By 2025, commercial sports betting revenue reached $16.96 billion and iGaming revenue reached $10.74 billion, creating a $27.70 billion commercial online-addressable market, up an estimated 24.6% from 2024. Growth is still strong, but the competitive story has shifted from pure state launches to retention, same-game parlays, iGaming cross-sell, tax-rate pressure and challenges from prediction markets, sweepstakes casinos and offshore operators.

key_stats.market_size: 2025 commercial online-addressable GGR of $27.70 billion, comprising $16.96 billion in sports betting revenue and $10.74 billion in iGaming revenue; sports betting includes some retail sportsbook revenue and excludes tribal/mobile Florida revenue.
key_stats.growth: 2025 market growth was an estimated 24.6% year over year, based on AGA-reported sports betting growth of 22.8% and iGaming growth of 27.6%.
key_stats.sports_betting_handle: 2025 commercial sports betting handle was $166.94 billion, up 11.0% from 2024.
key_stats.igaming_revenue: 2025 iGaming revenue was $10.74 billion, up 27.6% from 2024 across seven lawful online casino states.
key_stats.sports_betting_revenue: 2025 commercial sports betting revenue was $16.96 billion, up 22.8% from 2024.
key_stats.taxes: 2025 sports betting generated $3.71 billion in state-regulated taxes and iGaming generated $2.59 billion in taxes.
key_stats.legal_reach: As of July 2026, 38 states plus Washington, DC and Puerto Rico offered legal sports betting in some format, while 30 states plus DC and Puerto Rico allowed online sports betting.
key_stats.monthly_snapshot: In May 2026, sports betting revenue was $1.34 billion, down 1.8% year over year, while iGaming revenue was $1.03 billion, up 14.7% year over year.

baseline_2022.market_size: IBISWorld baseline revenue was $10.674 billion in 2022 dollars for 2022.
baseline_2022.growth: IBISWorld estimated 2022 revenue growth of 39.6% and a 2017-2022 revenue CAGR of 71.1%.
baseline_2022.profit: IBISWorld estimated 2022 industry profit at -$363 million, equal to a -3.4% margin.
baseline_2022.employment: IBISWorld estimated 26,861 employees and $2.034 billion in wages in 2022.
baseline_2022.enterprises: IBISWorld estimated 166 enterprises and 292 establishments in 2022.
baseline_2022.product_mix: IBISWorld estimated 2022 revenue mix at 49.7% online sports betting, 34.6% online gaming, 10.6% online poker and 5.1% other.

how_it_makes_money: Operators earn revenue from sportsbook hold, online casino win, poker rake or tournament fees, promotional breakage, affiliate arrangements and sometimes retail or fantasy-adjacent products. In 2025, the largest revenue pools were sportsbook GGR from $166.94 billion in commercial handle and iGaming GGR of $10.74 billion. The customer relationship is primarily app-based: operators acquire users through bonuses, media partnerships, league and team sponsorships, affiliate marketing and loyalty programs, then monetize through repeat wagering, parlays, in-play betting and casino cross-sell in states where iGaming is legal.
cost_structure: The largest costs are gaming taxes, player promotions, revenue share with market-access partners, payment processing, data and odds feeds, technology, compliance, fraud controls, geolocation, customer support and advertising. DraftKings reported 2025 cost of revenue of $3.56 billion, or 58.7% of revenue, plus $1.38 billion of sales and marketing and $459.9 million of product and technology expense. Flutter reported 2025 U.S. cost of sales equal to 56.8% of U.S. revenue, with gaming taxes adding pressure during 2025. BetMGM’s 2025 results show the operating leverage pattern: net revenue rose 33% to $2.80 billion while EBITDA improved to $220 million after a 2024 EBITDA loss of $244 million.
major_players: FanDuel / Flutter Entertainment: Flutter reported 2025 U.S. revenue of $6.967 billion, up 20% from 2024, and remains the leading national sportsbook brand.
DraftKings: 2025 revenue was $6.055 billion, up 27.0% from 2024; Sportsbook and iGaming revenue was $5.6 billion, up 27.7%.
BetMGM: 2025 net revenue was $2.796 billion, up 33%, including $1.827 billion from iGaming and $903 million from online sports.
Caesars Sportsbook: national omnichannel operator using Caesars Rewards, casino access and retail sportsbook relationships to compete in online wagering.
Fanatics Sportsbook: challenger brand expanding through the 2024 PointsBet U.S. acquisition and sports-merchandise customer relationships.
bet365, ESPN BET and regional/tribal brands: smaller but active competitors in selected online sports-betting states.
current_dynamics: The market is still expanding, but the easy phase of growth from first-wave legalization has slowed. Sports betting is broadly legal, so 2025-2026 growth increasingly comes from deeper engagement, higher hold, parlay mix, iGaming cross-sell and new products rather than a constant stream of large new state launches. Online casino is more profitable and faster growing, but it remains legal in far fewer states than sports betting. Operators are also navigating rising state tax rates, tighter advertising scrutiny, responsible-gaming obligations and gray-market competition from sweepstakes casinos, offshore sites and sports-event prediction markets. In May 2026, AGA data showed sports betting revenue down 1.8% year over year while iGaming rose 14.7%, highlighting the divergence between a maturing sportsbook market and a still-growing online casino market.
whats_growing: iGaming is growing fastest: 2025 revenue reached $10.74 billion, up 27.6%, and May 2026 iGaming revenue was $1.03 billion, up 14.7% year over year. Existing-state monetization is growing as operators reduce inefficient promotions and improve retention. BetMGM’s 2025 online sports net revenue rose 63% and iGaming net revenue rose 24%, while DraftKings’ 2025 Sportsbook and iGaming revenue rose 27.7%. Mobile-first wagering, same-game parlays, in-play betting, personalization and casino cross-sell are the strongest product growth lanes.
whats_shrinking: Promotional intensity is shrinking relative to the launch years as leading operators prioritize contribution profit and adjusted EBITDA. Retail sportsbook relevance is shrinking as most legal sports wagering shifts to mobile apps. The pool of unlegalized large sports-betting states is shrinking, which limits the future boost from new state launches. In 2026, regulated sportsbook growth is also being pressured by prediction-market competition; AGA reported May 2026 sports betting revenue down 1.8% year over year and said prediction markets were diverting activity outside state gaming-tax systems.
recent_developments: 2025-08: AGA estimated unregulated gaming devices, offshore sportsbooks and illegal online casinos generated $53.9 billion in annual revenue and caused more than $15 billion in lost state tax revenue.
2025-12-01: Missouri launched legal sports betting, with major mobile operators including FanDuel and DraftKings going live statewide.
2025-12-22: FanDuel and CME Group launched FanDuel Predicts in five states, starting a phased U.S. prediction-markets rollout.
2026-02-04: BetMGM reported 2025 net revenue of $2.796 billion, up 33%, and EBITDA of $220 million.
2026-02-26: AGA reported 2025 commercial sports betting revenue of $16.96 billion and iGaming revenue of $10.74 billion.
2026-03-20: FanDuel expanded into Arkansas through Oaklawn Sports, adding another online sportsbook market.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is positive but more uneven than the 2018-2024 launch cycle. Sports betting should keep growing in states with active mobile markets, but year-over-year gains are likely to moderate as mature markets lap large prior-year handle and operators face tax and promotion pressure. iGaming remains the larger margin opportunity because only a handful of states have legalized online casino; each new iGaming state can add a meaningful revenue pool. Industry profitability should improve for scaled leaders as marketing normalizes and technology costs are spread across larger player bases, but new-product investment, unfavorable sports outcomes, higher gaming taxes and prediction-market competition can interrupt margin gains. The strongest operators will be those with broad state access, high parlay and live-betting engagement, casino cross-sell, efficient promotions and credible responsible-gaming controls.

title: Online Greeting Card Sales
one_liner: Online greeting card sellers are benefiting from personalization, mobile ordering and digital gifting, but low entry barriers and offline card resilience keep pricing power limited.
overview: Online greeting card sales sit between e-commerce, publishing and digital media. Operators sell customized printed cards, mailed cards, e-cards, video greetings, invitations and bulk business cards through websites and apps. The baseline IBISWorld file put 2021 revenue at $1.289 billion and projected modest expansion to about $1.4 billion by 2026; newer 2025 market data for the broader U.S. greeting card market shows online channels accounting for 28.45% of a $7.12 billion market, implying roughly $2.03 billion of U.S. online-channel greeting card sales in 2025. Growth is faster online than offline, but the category remains seasonal and crowded, with Hallmark, American Greetings, Paperless Post, Minted, Shutterfly, Etsy sellers and many niche design shops competing on design variety, convenience, subscription access, delivery speed and personalization.

key_stats.market_size: 2025: approximately $2.03 billion in U.S. online-channel greeting card sales, calculated from Grand View Research's $7.12 billion U.S. greeting card market and 28.45% online distribution share.
key_stats.growth: 2026-2033: online U.S. greeting card sales expected to grow at a 3.6% CAGR, compared with 1.6% CAGR for the total U.S. greeting card market.
key_stats.business_count: 2024: 2,491 U.S. online greeting card sales businesses, up 11.9% from 2023, according to IBISWorld.
key_stats.online_share: 2025: online distribution represented 28.45% of U.S. greeting card sales, while offline represented 71.55%.
key_stats.profit_margin: 2021: 6.2% EBIT margin in the IBISWorld baseline; 2026 baseline projection: 5.5% as competition and marketing costs rise.

baseline_2022.market_size: 2022: approximately $1.32 billion, inferred from the IBISWorld baseline's 2021 revenue of $1.289 billion and its 2021-2026 projected CAGR of 2.1%.
baseline_2022.growth: 2022: approximately 2.1% projected annual growth based on the IBISWorld baseline outlook.
baseline_2022.business_count: 2022: approximately 1,690 enterprises implied by IBISWorld's later 2023 count of 2,227 and 2024 count of 2,491, though the baseline file's older 2021 forecast expected 1,728 enterprises by 2026.

how_it_makes_money: Revenue comes from single customized cards, seasonal cards, bulk personal or corporate orders, e-card subscriptions, premium templates, app memberships, print-and-mail fulfillment fees, delivery add-ons, digital gift card attachments, advertising-supported free-card traffic and branded corporate greeting programs.
cost_structure: Major costs include printing and card stock for physical orders, postage and fulfillment, payment processing, software development, cloud hosting, licensing for characters or celebrity video greetings, graphic design labor, customer service, digital marketing, affiliate traffic acquisition and marketplace commissions. The baseline file put 2021 wages at $272.9 million and profit at $80 million, or a 6.2% EBIT margin, with wages projected to reach $337.3 million by 2026 and margin to fall to 5.5% as competition intensifies.
current_dynamics: The online channel is outgrowing the overall greeting-card market because consumers can personalize cards, send instantly, schedule reminders and attach digital gifts. At the same time, the total market remains anchored by physical cards bought in stores, especially for holidays and last-minute occasions. Operators are layering subscriptions, celebrity/video greetings, AI writing help, mobile apps and print-and-mail options onto what was once a simple card catalog. Competition is fragmented because creators can enter through Etsy, Canva, Shopify and print-on-demand tools, while incumbents use brands, licensing, retail distribution and loyalty programs to defend share.
whats_growing: Fastest-growing pockets include digital e-cards, mobile-first card creation, subscription access, AI-assisted copy and design, personalized photo cards, video greetings, digital gift-card attachments, corporate appreciation cards, online invitations with RSVP tools and premium artist-designed cards sold through omnichannel distribution.
whats_shrinking: Undifferentiated bulk printed cards, low-personalization seasonal cards, purely advertising-supported free e-card sites and casual card purchases that can be replaced by texts, social posts or messaging-app stickers are under pressure. Offline still dominates total U.S. greeting-card sales in 2025, but its share is gradually giving ground to online ordering and digital delivery.
recent_developments: 2024-09: IBISWorld reported 2,491 U.S. online greeting-card sales businesses in 2024, up 11.9% from 2023.
2024-10: Hallmark launched Gift Card Greetings, combining a physical card with a redeemable digital gift card from more than 100 brands.
2025-02: Elliott Investment Management closed its acquisition of a majority stake in American Greetings, with CD&R and the Weiss family retaining minority ownership.
2025-02: American Greetings expanded digital gifting in e-cards with retail gift cards, cash, experience vouchers and custom Songfinch songs.
2025-12: Minted announced its artist-designed greeting cards would be available in select Whole Foods Market stores across more than 520 U.S. locations.
2026-06: Grand View Research estimated the U.S. greeting card market at $7.12 billion in 2025 and projected online-channel growth at a 3.6% CAGR from 2026 to 2033.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is modestly positive. Online greeting card sales should keep gaining share from offline because convenience, personalization and instant delivery fit consumer behavior, while subscriptions and digital gifting raise order value. Growth is unlikely to be explosive because card sending is mature, highly seasonal and vulnerable to free digital substitutes. Margin pressure should remain elevated as incumbents and small sellers spend on search, social ads, creator content, licensed designs and app features. The winners are likely to be platforms that combine emotional design quality with fast fulfillment, reminders, AI message help and easy gift attachment.
one_sentence: The U.S. online greeting card sales industry sells physical cards ordered online and digital e-cards, with 2025 demand supported by e-commerce adoption, subscriptions, AI-assisted messages and last-minute digital gifting.
